rationale: Greek loanword παίδευσις 'training, discipline, education.' Central organizing term of this kephalaion (6 occurrences). The Apostle teaches that the παίδευσις at metarrismos (the disciplinary correction of catechumens at death-transformation) is paralleled by the παίδευσις given to children in the world. Retained as transliteration to mark its technical role; English 'training/discipline' would obscure the loanword's specific philosophical-pedagogical register.

Greek παιδεύειν 'to train, instruct, discipline.' Verbal counterpart to ⲡⲁⲓⲁⲉⲩⲥⲓⲥ above. Used twice on this page (lines 19, 27) for parental training of children. Standard Coptic '+ Greek loan' pattern.

Lycopolitan ⲁⲛ- ('in,' = Sah. ϩⲛ̄-) + ⲭⲱⲱⲙⲉ ('books,' Lyc. for ϫⲱⲱⲙⲉ). The disciples cite Mani's written corpus (the canonical Manichaean books) as authoritative source: 'you have proclaimed to us, you have written it for us in books.' Standard Manichaean self-reference to the apostle's writings.

Apparent Coptic abbreviation/transliteration of Greek κύριος 'lord, master.' Distinct from the more common Lycopolitan ⲡⲁⲭⲁⲓ̈ⲥ (= ⲡϫⲟⲉⲓⲥ, in glossary). May reflect a Greek-loaned title in the discipleship-frame opening the Apostle's reply. Confidence moderate — could alternatively be a different word entirely.

Hapax in this corpus. Context (introducing the Apostle's spoken response to the disciples' question) demands a verb of speech-response. Possibly a Lycopolitan/scribal variant of ⲁ⸗ϥ-ⲟⲩⲱϣⲃ-ⲟⲩ 'he answered them' with metathesis or contraction. Alternatively could be from a verb of declaring/addressing. Confidence low; flagged for parallel research.

Lycopolitan reflex of ⲧⲥⲏϥⲉ 'the sword' (regular Lyc ⲏⲩⲉ for ⲏϥⲉ; cf. ⲥⲟⲁⲡⲉⲧ for ⲥⲡⲟⲧⲟⲩ). Functions metaphorically here as the disciplinary instrument: 'one is the sword of the sons, one is the sword of the young ones.' Distinct from ⲡⲥⲁⲡ 'the sword' (in glossary, K.81 register).

Lycopolitan verb of unclear precise root. Context: 'the time when the son ⲩⲱϩⲧ' triggers parental discipline. Most plausible: Lyc. variant of ⲡⲱϩⲧ̄ 'fall, cast' (with ⲩ for ⲡ) yielding 'falls (into sin/error).' Alternatives: ϣⲟⲩϩⲧ̄ 'fail,' ϣⲱϩⲧ̄ 'kindle.' Confidence low; flagged for parallels.

proposed_english: marvel / spectacle (in compound ⲣ̄-ⲉⲡⲡⲏⲣⲉ 'make an example of')
rationale: Lycopolitan form related to ϣⲡⲏⲣⲉ 'wonder, marvel.' The compound ⲣ̄-ⲉⲡⲡⲏⲣⲉ 'do a wonder, make a spectacle' applied to disciplinary correction = 'make an example of (the offender) before others.' Doubled -ⲡⲡ- is unusual; possibly reflects ⲣ̄(ⲡ)-ⲉⲡⲡⲏⲣⲉ or scribal variant.

Already in glossary as 'transformation' (Greek μεταρρυθμισμός 'rearrangement, refashioning'). On this page (8 occurrences) the term carries a specifically eschatological-soteriological sense: the cosmic re-fashioning that powers effect upon souls departing the body, which both sinners (with mercy and measure) and catechumens (with hope) undergo. Confirms the technical force of the term beyond its earlier cosmological-flux usage.
